Emmett points out that
Kaczynski writes:

"The point is, if the ruling party were to leave office tomorrow, at least
according 
to TK, leftists would find something new 
to complain about.

Kaczynski also talks about the leftist's 
perceived need:

"to his satify his drive for power
by imposing his solutions on society."

It's Kaczynski who seems to be doing most
of the complaining.  He complains
about something that, as a matter
of logic, is inevitable unless there
were the most stringent controls.
He is the one evidencing "a need 
to satisfy a drive for power."
It is a matter of common sense
that if all the factories were destroyed
and books burned as he insists must 
be done,  that there would be no
way to suppress the emergence
of technology anew absent such
social controls.  That's why his central
thesis is such crock.  And given
that his bottom-line is so stupid
and irrational, as much as I'm attracted
to the arguments dressing his main
idea up, I wouldn't want to be seen
around town with them.
